project_specification.project_name: nullius — cost-aware discovery, commit and exploration (M2 pivot)
project_specification.addition_summary: The M2 baseline over 25 archive campaigns (docs/user-journeys/_run-log.md, Run 10 addendum 2) shows a cost blind spot: - Committed picks have in-sample IC t of about 3.8, but weekly turnover of 0.66. - Out of sample over 60 weeks, IC t is positive 25/25 (mean 0.57), while the cost-adjusted IR is negative 23/25. Selection is cost-blind everywhere: - close-out discovers and commits on ic_tstat >= 2 (orchestrator/closeout.py ~:753, ~:994) - the fixed exploration policy values live-tree nodes by ic_mean (orchestrator/_live_tree.py, read by BaselinePolicy in _policy.py) PRD G1 asks for positive cost-adjusted out-of-sample IR, and §2.3's M2 row says to revisit horizons against the cost model before M3. This spec makes every selection point cost-aware and shows agents what costs do, so M2 can be re-measured.

existing_context.test_baseline: main at 1061e8e: gate 1663 passed; orchestrator 576 passed 5 skipped.
existing_context.conventions: Follow CLAUDE.md. - NodeMetrics carries ir_standalone (the mean over the population standard deviation of per-date post-cost book returns), dates (its count) and turnover. - The node table has ic_mean, ic_tstat, ir_standalone, ir_marginal, turnover, cost_adjusted_ir and perturb_stability (0114). Node columns are added by probe-then-ALTER (see tripwires node_metric, F240's fail_class). - The live tree payload (_live_tree.py) reads id, parent_id, depth and ic_mean. - signal-agent's authoring prompt pairs each prior proposal with its recorded ScoreRecord (_llm_author.py _pair_scores ~:636).

category.name: Cost-Aware Selection
category.feature: System persists every evaluated node's post-cost IR t-statistic, so that a node row returns ir_tstat = ir_standalone · √(dates) beside ic_tstat. - The node table gains ir_tstat REAL NULL, added by probe-then-ALTER in the tree writer. The live store upgrades in place. - evaluate_node writes ir_tstat = metrics.ir_standalone · √(metrics.dates) on the node row, computed once from the metrics the pipeline measured. The ScoreRecord and the node_evaluated event carry it. - A failed node writes NULL. - test_post_cost_tstat.py covers: - the value equals ir_standalone·√dates for a scored node - a pre-existing node table upgrades in place - a failed node has NULL - the event carries the field It passes under pytest-xdist.

System discovers and commits on post-cost IR at close-out, so that `./run.sh closeout` returns discoveries and a committed pick chosen by cost-adjusted evidence, not rank IC alone. - A node is a discovery when ir_tstat >= DISCOVERY_TSTAT (2.0) and ic_tstat > 0. The same rule feeds sensitivity, specificity and FDR_deploy. - The commit is the eligible node with the highest ir_tstat. Ties are broken by node id. A miss is unchanged. - A node row with no ir_tstat (a store from before feature 1) falls back to the IC rule. The JSON line names which rule ran: selection_rule "post-cost-ir" or "ic-fallback". - The previous IC-based discovery count is kept as a diagnostic: discoveries_ic. - The KS gate's non-significance filter keeps using ic_tstat. It is about detectability, not cost, and is unchanged. - test_closeout_cost_aware.py covers: - a high-IC, high-turnover node with negative ir_tstat is not a discovery - the commit picks the highest ir_tstat - the fallback applies when ir_tstat is absent - discoveries_ic is reported - the Type-R and Type-D paths both use the new rule It passes under pytest-xdist. The orchestrator member suite passes.

System gives the exploration policy each node's post-cost evidence, so that the fixed baseline's select() returns a batch ranked by post-cost IR t-statistic. - The live tree payload carries ir_tstat beside ic_mean, read by the same query. - The value the baseline policy ranks by is ir_tstat when present. Otherwise it is ic_mean, as before. The value field is renamed in one place only if the policy-runtime view requires a single `value`; it is documented. - The prefix view and determinism contracts are unchanged. - test_live_tree_cost_value.py covers: - a node with a higher ic_mean but lower ir_tstat ranks below its sibling - the absent ir_tstat fallback - determinism of the batch It passes under pytest-xdist.

System tells the authoring agent how costs judge its signal, so that the model returns signals designed for a post-cost book rather than for rank IC. - The rendered authoring prompt displays: - the node is scored and selected on the post-cost IR t-statistic of a dollar-neutral book rebalanced on the evaluation grid - the grid's cadence, read from the evaluation context (weekly for the archive configs) - the cost model's per-rebalance cost (fees plus spread assumption, as bps of traded notional) and how turnover multiplies it - Each prior proposal in the context shows ic_tstat, ir_tstat, turnover and cost_adjusted_ir from its recorded score, where present. - The rendered prompt displays one line of guidance: high turnover erodes the post-cost book, and persistent or smoothed signals with lower turnover are preferred when their IC survives. It judges nothing and is information only. - Every other rendered prompt section is byte-identical to before (a test compares the sections outside the new ones). Prompt-keyed recorded fixtures are regenerated only if they pin the changed sections, and the commit message says so. - test_prompt_cost_awareness.py covers: - the rendered prompt contains the cadence and the per-rebalance cost from a fixture context - prior proposals show the four figures - the absent-figure path renders "unmeasured" It passes under pytest-xdist. The signal-agent member suite passes.
